rows.test: W1 repair
rows.result: Pass by its registered test: meta repair fixes 100% of trials vs 50% for local reflect-and-retry (0% vs 100% on cross-agent faults); fails the baseline audit (ties the equal-information greedy baseline)
rows.meaning: The gain comes from the global view: an equal-information greedy baseline also fixes 100%, so the loop itself adds nothing measured here (results/baseline_audit.md)

rows.test: W4 safety
rows.result: Pass: 350/350 attempts blocked and logged, 0/350 legitimate proposals blocked
rows.meaning: Rules are wired in; not a test against an adaptive adversary

rows.test: H-CFIT / H-SWITCH
rows.result: Pass by its registered test: ledger-estimated switching beats rule, rotation, fixed (Lion) and the bandit on the registered reward; fails the baseline audit (loses to one fixed archetype chosen by a 20-person pilot, Bear: −0.011 per tick [−0.012, −0.010])
rows.meaning: Small margins; final distress is worse than under the rule. Staying in the stabilising archetype throughout does better than switching (results/baseline_audit.md)

rows.test: W3 transfer
rows.meaning: Same-named archetypes do different jobs on agents and on people; a function-based mapping (W3b) is a new hypothesis

rows.test: G1, the gate on the W3 tables
rows.result: Pass in both directions by its registered test; fails the baseline audit (identical to transferring nothing)
rows.meaning: Every harmful entry was blocked; gated transfer is never worse than none and beats ungated transfer by +0.023 to +0.061 per tick. The gate rejected every entry in both directions, so the gated tables equal "transfer nothing" (results/baseline_audit.md)

rows.test: G2, a case where transfer can be valid
rows.meaning: Still no harm (gated beats ungated by +0.050 to +0.147), but nothing was admitted, so no gain; the sources proposed archetypes by name, and the substrates share roles instead

rows.test: H-CFIT under the mission score
rows.result: Pass by its registered test; fails the baseline audit (loses to fixed Bear chosen by a 20-person pilot: −0.085 per tick [−0.095, −0.074])
rows.meaning: Beats rule, rotation, fixed (Lion) and bandit by +0.09 to +0.16 per tick; final distress 3.58 (was 6.80 under the old score). Fixed Bear scores +0.129 per tick against the watchdog's +0.045 (results/baseline_audit.md)

rows.test: W3b, role-based transfer (AGENTS.md §11.3)
rows.meaning: Roles were read correctly in 12 of 12 runs, but the gate starved on a uniform pilot and per-context policies flickered; "restore always" reaches near-oracle on the person and agents v1 but not on agents v2 (results/w3b.md)

rows.test: W3c, policy-level transfer tested as deployed (AGENTS.md §11.4, fourth attempt)
rows.meaning: Safe in every case; useful in one direction of four (person → agents v1: at 16 pilot targets adopted 13/20 times against 1/20 for pilot-only, +0.047 per tick); the best policy differs by substrate (results/w3c.md)

rows.test: W5, transfer through the R4 layers (AGENTS.md §11.5, fifth attempt)
rows.meaning: Certificates were accurate (0 false of 27), but the failure-driven pilot starved the gate; alternating in every context did better (results/w5.md)

rows.test: W5-R, failure repurposing vs repair (§11.5)
rows.meaning: Agents: beats repair and random change in 2 of 3 held-out regimes, more spikes in the trigger storm; persons: no mechanism admitted. 34,000 failure nodes, none closed silently (results/w5r.md)

rows.test: LIA-G, genealogy recovery (§11.5)
rows.meaning: F1 0.12; beats temporal proximity but not random; causes diagnosed (results/lia_g.md)

rows.test: C1–C6, corpus lineage (§11.5)
rows.result: C4 pass, C3 fail, C1/C2/C5 not testable, C6 inconclusive
rows.meaning: Output re-entering as the next prompt is the strong signal (results/corpus_lineage.md; summary results/r6_summary.md)

rows.test: W5b, transfer with a full pilot (§11.6, sixth attempt)
rows.meaning: Two directions beat pilot-only, no transfer and random functions for the first time; 0.06 more spikes per target than pilot-only in one direction blocked the pass (results/w5b.md)
rows.parent: W5, transfer through the R4 layers (AGENTS.md §11.5, fifth attempt)

rows.test: W5-R2, repurposing with probe and spike guard (§11.6)
rows.meaning: Persons: equal to doing nothing, better than repair and random change (a do-no-harm pass); agents: untested commits hurt (results/w5r2.md)
F1 0.12; beats temporal and random (results/lia_g2.md)

rows.test: Corpus v2 (§11.6)
rows.result: R1, R2, C4b pass; C1b, C6b inconclusive
rows.meaning: Output re-enters as input and carries forward more than the person's own words (results/corpus_v2.md; summary results/r6b_summary.md)

rows.test: W5c, transfer with pilot spike guard (§11.7, seventh attempt)
rows.meaning: Agents v1 → person meets every condition including safety; a second direction is needed (results/w5c.md)
rows.parent: W5b, transfer with a full pilot (§11.6, sixth attempt)

rows.test: W5-R3, every change probed (§11.7)
rows.meaning: The non-harm probe rejects almost every library mechanism; the trained policies leave the fixed library nothing to improve (results/w5r3.md)
rows.parent: W5-R2, repurposing with probe and spike guard (§11.6)

rows.meaning: 8 committed changes in 1,200 runs; not a meaningful test (results/lia_g3.md; summary results/r6c_summary.md)

rows.test: T-AP, transfer agents v1 → person (§11.8)
rows.result: PASS, confirmed by its registered test; fails the baseline audit (loses to a source-free rule in both runs: −0.133 and −0.140 per tick)
rows.meaning: Beats pilot-only by +0.024 per tick with fewer spikes, and holds on new seeds and a second person model (results/tap.md). But the target's stabilising archetype everywhere, read from the same pilot with no source, scores +0.244 against T-AP's +0.111, so this is not evidence that anything transferred (results/baseline_audit.md)

rows.test: W5d, negative certificates + fail-safe tube (§11.8)
rows.meaning: Two directions beat every comparator; one has slightly more spikes than pilot-only; the jam predictor is near chance (results/w5d.md)
rows.parent: W5c, transfer with pilot spike guard (§11.7, seventh attempt)

rows.test: W5-R4, anticipatory forge (§11.8)
rows.meaning: The Lion's failure forecasts beat the base rate on agents; the 10-tick ghost passes carry too little evidence (results/w5r4.md; summary results/r6d_summary.md)

rows.test: T-AP-4 / T-AP-V2, reach of the confirmed transfer (§11.9)
rows.meaning: Pilot 4 passes on person model v1, not on v2; agents v2 → person does not transfer (results/tapr.md)

rows.test: J1, jam predictor (§11.9)
rows.result: Accepted (passed its registered test); fails the baseline audit (not significantly above never-jam: exact McNemar p = 0.054 against the registered 0.01)
rows.meaning: 0.754 accuracy on fresh seeds against 0.685 for always predicting "no jam" (results/j1.md) (results/baseline_audit.md)
Two directions beat every comparator; person → agents v1 adds spikes again (results/w5e.md)

rows.test: W5-R5, snapshot forge (§11.9)
rows.result: Fail (agents: beats repair, random and doing nothing in 2 of 3 regimes; below doing nothing after the mid-run shift)
rows.meaning: First time repurposing improves on doing nothing; the mechanisms the failures shaped carried it (results/w5r5.md; summary results/r6e_summary.md)

rows.test: W5-R6, snapshot forge with re-verification (§11.10)
rows.meaning: Agents: beats every comparator in the fault storm only; re-verification lifts the shift regime by +0.016 but stays just below doing nothing; round 5's E2 gain did not replicate (results/w5r6.md; summary results/r6f_summary.md)

rows.test: Phase 9 public-data replication, WildChat-1M shards 0–2 (§11.11)
rows.meaning: R1, R3, MSE notes, MSE phrases and C2 pass; MSE melody fails as a scale (carry-forward does not clear, as at the origin); C5 fails. First LSGPA result replicated outside the private record (results/p9.md; summary results/p9_summary.md)

rows.test: Round 7 person model v3 and safety recall on a consented private record (§11.12)
rows.meaning: Neither hand-set nor fitted dynamics beat "next state = current"; the safety rules are right given a perfect reading, but a keyword reader catches 13% of the moments that call for them (results/r7.md)

rows.test: SR-2 meaning-based reader for the safety layer (§11.13)
rows.meaning: Any-screen recall 0.81 (from 0.13) with no false alarms, but not every critical turn: the misses share one kind of wording that the registered definition left unsettled (details private) (results/sr2.md)

rows.test: SR-3 past high-distress check-in and fixed definition (§11.14)
rows.meaning: Recall 0.95, 1 false alarm in 270, every check-in turn answered with a check-in; the one miss came from a condition in the §3.1 rule, since fixed (details private) (results/sr3.md)

rows.test: LIA-WW lineage attribution on real multi-agent failure logs, Who&When (§11.15)
rows.meaning: Same model, same logs: the first-failure rule finds the responsible agent as well as all-at-once judging (69.6% vs 67.4%) but the decisive step slightly less often (41.8% vs 45.1%); it helps on long hand-crafted logs (results/lia_ww.md)

rows.test: W5-CEILING, perfect source knowledge vs an 8-target pilot (spec/CEILING.md)
rows.result: Analysis: the W5 transfer line stops in all four directions (spec/FIXES_P2.md C1–C3)
rows.meaning: By the registered rule agent → person passes: perfect source knowledge beats an 8-target pilot by +0.213 per tick. That room cannot be credited to the source: a source-free rule (the target's stabilising archetype everywhere, read from the pilot's own ticks) reaches the same +0.240 (review P2-1). person → agent: no better than the pilot; agent v2 → person: no value; person → agent v2: harmful (−0.050). No successor is planned; any future transfer test needs a source-free arm (results/ceiling.md)

rows.test: H-CTX, context-dependent reply style in real arena votes (spec/CTX_PREF.md)
rows.meaning: Only 128 of 35,858 real prompts described a personal difficulty, too few to test the context that matters most. Length-matched, neither stabilising acknowledgment nor asking back wins or loses clearly anywhere (results/ctx_pref.md)

rows.test: H-CTX2, the same question on hh-rlhf helpfulness pairs (spec/CTX_PREF_HH.md)
rows.meaning: 505 of 123,415 prompts were personal, with 11 and 22 usable pairs (50 needed). In everyday prompts, replies that end by asking back were chosen less often (0.413). Information only: the stabilising reply was chosen in 9 of 11 personal pairs (results/ctx_pref_hh.md)

rows.test: H-CTX3, the same question in WildChat-1M by the person's next reaction (spec/CTX_PREF_WC.md)
rows.meaning: 536,786 real reactions, but only 185 stabilising replies to personal messages (200 needed). In everyday requests, replies that end by asking back are followed by worse reactions (−0.011 [−0.020, −0.002]), as in H-CTX2. Association, not cause (results/ctx_pref_wc.md)

rows.test: Corpus lineage across conversations, ADOPT-WC: do the AI's words become the person's own across conversations (spec/ADOPT_WC.md)
rows.meaning: 26,783 persons in WildChat-1M: the AI's new words from the previous conversation appeared in the person's next opening message less often than placebo words from the following conversation (-0.0046 [-0.0059, -0.0032]). The placebo is likely inflated by the AI echoing the person; not shown by this design, rather than shown absent (results/adopt_wc.md)

rows.test: Round 8, the Person Lab: 100 profiles from ESConv, step 5 validation (spec/PERSONLAB.md)
rows.meaning: Profiles built with agreement kappa 0.728 (passes). But the simulated persons do not predict final intensity better than a linear baseline (0.81 against 0.68), the fit gives every support strategy the same effect, and the profile makes the prediction worse (results/personlab_step5.json)

rows.test: Round 8b, stress per turn and the profile-targeted override (spec/PERSONLAB.md §7b)
rows.meaning: Stress read reliably from 1,584 turns (weighted kappa 0.925). But supporters addressed the person's own belief or identity wording in only 3 of 560 moments (30 needed) (results/personlab_step5b.json)

rows.test: Round 8c, do the stress readings track people's own ratings (spec/PERSONLAB.md §7c)
rows.meaning: Not valid: reader stress against the seekers' own intensity gives ρ 0.21 (start), 0.11 (end) and 0.03 (change). Readers appear to track a message's tone, such as polite greetings and thanks, more than how the person reports feeling; with 100 conversations the intervals are wide, so a weak link is not ruled out (results/personlab_step5c.json)

rows.test: Round 8d, VAKOG matching and echo against people's own ratings (spec/RAPPORT_ESCONV.md)
rows.meaning: No effect shown on 6,970 ratings (a small benefit of matching is not ruled out): matching the person's sensory channel +0.09 [-0.02, +0.20], echoing their words -0.02 [-0.09, +0.05] on the 1–5 rating; both together not testable (96 events) (results/rapport_esconv.json)

rows.test: Round 8e, supporter action against the seeker's next rating of the support (spec/TURN_RATINGS.md)
rows.meaning: 6,352 rated events in ESConv (crowdworkers playing seekers). The supporter's action did not measurably improve the prediction of the seeker's next rating of the support beyond the previous rating, stage and starting intensity: −0.0008 [−0.0036, +0.0019] in mean squared error, inside the ±0.01 equivalence band; letting it depend on stage did not either (+0.0032 [+0.0005, +0.0063]). An association. A per-action effect above about 0.1–0.2 rating points would have shown (the review's sensitivity check, not registered). The previous rating and start beat persistence by −0.185 [−0.232, −0.141] (results/turn_ratings.json)

rows.test: Round 8f, person model v3: a cue resolves on its own after 6 ticks (spec/CUE_RESOLVE.md)
rows.meaning: Stuck cues under always Bear fall from 15 of 15 runs to 0, but ticks with a cue open fall only 1.8×, because about 15× more cues now arrive. With the loophole closed, always Bear still beats the Watchdog (−0.0193 [−0.0266, −0.0115] per tick on 200 fresh persons), but that lead comes entirely from the Watchdog meeting about 11% more cues: on all other ticks the Watchdog is ahead (+0.0143 [+0.0042, +0.0241]; the review's decomposition, reproduced). Not evidence that stabilising helps. Stated models (results/cue_resolve.json, results/cue_resolve_decomp.json)

rows.test: Round 8f-B, is person model v3 adopted: is cue exposure the same under every policy? (spec/CUE_RESOLVE.md §8)
rows.result: Analysis (criterion set after its answer; half of it holds by construction)
rows.meaning: On 200 fresh persons, cues per person under always Bear, the Watchdog and Lion are 9.6, 10.6 and 9.6 on v3, against 1.0, 5.5 and 1.0 on v2. Neither Bear nor Lion ever interrupts a cue, so their exposure is set by the trigger rate and R alone. v3 is available; adopting it is the author's decision (FIXES_NIGHT FB-1). Stated models (results/cue_resolve_adopt.json)
